doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His mother Jeanette and the song "Stormy Monday"
summary: His mother wrote poetry and says she wrote "Stormy Monday", selling it to T-Bone Walker for 50 dollars.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So my mother Jeanette used to write poetry and she actually was the original composer of “Stormy Monday,” and she wrote that. We knew T-Bone Walker. She sold it to T-Bone Walker for 50 bucks, so that became a big hit! You know, those days musicians used to sell, they used to buy, they'd sell songs. Jazz musicians would say, "Hey, I need a tune for a record date, send me a tune," and they would put their name on it. They'd buy a song, so that's what happened.
Does she have any other credits that we might know of?
Well hey, all it takes is one…
